submission:
Root cause: The board does not establish a cause for the 17:38:25 onset. The only concrete anomaly is a ~4-second burst of Consul discovery refusals on consul:8500 right after frontend's cold start at 17:31:56 [tr_141f2b9c494c][tr_b46c4a6267a3], a bootstrap race between the frontend and consul workloads both first created at 17:31:55 by platform-automation [tr_57fd4b831076][tr_c4d033b6d797]. That burst ended at 17:32:00 and never recurred, leaving ~6.5 clean minutes before the alert [tr_b46c4a6267a3], so it is not the onset mechanism. Everything that could name the real mechanism was structurally unavailable: no span metrics for frontend or user in either window [tr_9e57cb00ad61][tr_3c200821e5c6], zero frontend traces for the hour [tr_e4ec257e6a74], and a truncated log slice covering only 17:31:56-17:32:00 [tr_141f2b9c494c]. The fault most likely lies on one of the five unmeasured edges below frontend, unidentified.
Faulty component: frontend
Fault type: unknown
Confidence: low

Evidence:
- Consul connection-refused lines on port 8500 from frontend are confined to a ~4-second burst immediately following the 17:31:56 cold start, with the last occurrence at 17:32:00; no further 8500 lines appear through the end of the window at 17:38:30. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- The same cold start emitted the frontend's consul agent initialization and address-read lines at 17:31:56, confirming the refused attempts are startup-time discovery lookups against the consul service VIP rather than steady-state traffic. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- The refused lookups covered all five downstream services (user, recommendation, search, profile, reservation), indicating a whole-dependency outage of the Consul endpoint during that burst, not a single-service registration problem. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- No 8500-matching lines appear in the ~23 minutes of the window preceding the cold start (17:08:25 to 17:31:56), so discovery was not failing before the restart. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- Consul discovery failures persisted from the cold start through to the 17:38:25 onset and are the direct cause of the incident. (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: The query covers the full window and is not truncated; the last 8500 refused line is at 17:32:00, leaving roughly six and a half minutes of clean discovery before onset.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- Discovery was already degraded before the restart, making the cold start a symptom of an earlier Consul problem. (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: No 8500 lines at all are present between the window start at 17:08:25 and the 17:31:56 initialization.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- A single downstream service failed to register in Consul, starving one dependency. (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: All five srv-* lookups failed identically within the same burst, which points at the Consul endpoint being unreachable rather than per-service registration.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- Frontend was pointed at a wrong or stale Consul address, causing chronic connection refusals. (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: The same address and VIP that produced refusals at 17:31:56 stopped producing them by 17:32:00 without any further address-read line, so the configured target became reachable.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"} |= "8500")
- The only error-level text emitted by frontend in the returned lines is a repeated service-discovery failure: the Consul load-balancer client cannot retrieve instances from the Consul agent, with the HTTP GET to the Consul health endpoint failing as a refused TCP connection to the cluster IP on port 8500. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The failures span every backend the frontend resolves (user, recommendation, profile, search, reservation), indicating the fault is at the discovery dependency rather than specific to one downstream service. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The frontend pod went through a full cold start at 17:31:56 (config read, Jaeger init, Consul agent init, gRPC client init, HTTP serving), so the process restarted inside the alert window rather than running continuously. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Despite the discovery errors, the frontend completed startup and began serving HTTP ~1s later, so the process stayed up and kept retrying rather than crash-looping on this error. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Returned lines are clustered in roughly 17:31:56–17:32:00 and the result is marked truncated, so coverage of the full 17:08–17:38 window is not established. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Frontend is failing due to a panic, nil dereference, or other crash in its own application code (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: No panic, stack trace, or fatal-level entry appears; the sole error class is the Consul discovery call, and the process reaches its serving state.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- A specific downstream hotel-reservation service (e.g. search or reservation) is returning errors and dragging frontend down (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: The errors are not gRPC call failures against those services; they are failures to look the services up at all, and they affect every backend uniformly.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- DNS resolution for the Consul service is broken (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: The Consul hostname resolves to a cluster IP in the error text; the failure mode is a refused connection at that address, not a lookup failure.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- TLS or certificate misconfiguration on the frontend is blocking its dependencies (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: Startup logs record TLS as disabled and report no certificate or handshake errors; the dependency failure is a plain refused TCP connection.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Frontend failed to start or is stuck before binding its listener (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: The startup sequence completes and the HTTP serving line is emitted seconds after boot.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Only two change records exist for consul in the 24-hour window, both timestamped identically at 17:31:55 roughly six minutes before onset: a service-level config creation and a first-ever container/workload creation, both attributed to the platform-automation actor. (found, from change_history on consul)
- The pairing of a service creation with a 'first created' workload indicates this was an initial stand-up of the Consul agent/server rather than a modification of an already-running instance, placing a brand-new deployment immediately upstream of onset. (found, from change_history on consul)
- No change activity is recorded for consul in the hours preceding 17:31:55, so the entire earlier portion of the window is change-free for this service. (found, from change_history on consul)
- A configuration edit or parameter change to an existing, previously healthy Consul deployment regressed it and triggered the incident. (ruled_out, from change_history on consul; why: The only config record is a creation, not an update, and it is paired with a first-time container creation — there was no prior running instance for a config change to regress.)
- A restart loop or repeated crash-restart cycle of the Consul agent explains the symptoms. (ruled_out, from change_history on consul; why: No restart events appear anywhere in the 24-hour window; the only container event is a single first creation.)
- The orchestrator rescheduled or evicted the Consul workload onto a different node, causing disruption. (ruled_out, from change_history on consul; why: No rescheduling, eviction, or migration events are recorded; the single container event is an initial creation with no predecessor placement.)
- A slow-acting change made hours earlier drifted into failure around onset. (ruled_out, from change_history on consul; why: The window contains no change activity before 17:31:55, so there is no earlier change to have drifted.)
- A human operator made an ad-hoc manual change to Consul shortly before onset. (ruled_out, from change_history on consul; why: Both recorded changes are attributed to the platform-automation actor, not a human operator.)

Reasoning:
Frontend's own code is cleared: no panic or fatal entry, and the process reached its serving state [tr_141f2b9c494c]. No deploy, flag flip, config edit, restart or human action touched frontend or consul beyond initial creation [tr_57fd4b831076][tr_c4d033b6d797], removing bad_deploy, feature_flag and a regressing config edit. A wrong Consul address is excluded because the same address stopped refusing without any re-read [tr_b46c4a6267a3]. What remains - a quiet, running frontend alerting six minutes after discovery recovered - cannot be resolved because metrics, traces and the onset-minute logs are all missing [tr_9e57cb00ad61][tr_e4ec257e6a74][tr_3c200821e5c6]. Naming a class here would be asserting past the evidence.

Alternatives considered:
1. consul: Consul remained unhealthy or degraded after its 17:31:55 stand-up, so frontend's later re-resolutions stalled and callers waited. (dependency_latency). Ranked lower because: The 8500-filtered query covered the full window without truncation and shows no refusals after 17:32:00 [tr_b46c4a6267a3]; no Consul-side log or metric was ever gathered to support ongoing degradation.
2. user: A downstream hotel-reservation service became slow after 17:32, and frontend's requests failed on waiting for it. (dependency_latency). Ranked lower because: Zero traces and no span metrics exist to attribute latency to any downstream service [tr_e4ec257e6a74][tr_3c200821e5c6]; this is a plausible shape with no evidence naming a culprit.

Open questions:
- What did frontend log between 17:32:00 and 17:38:30? The unfiltered query was truncated and never covered the onset minute.
- Which of the five unmeasured downstream edges (user, recommendation, profile, search, reservation) was slow or erroring at onset? No per-service logs or latency data were gathered for any of them.
- Is Consul itself healthy after 17:32:00? Its own logs and health were never queried - only its change history.
